integrity: The infinite claim is proved by an intrinsic core recovery, exact orbit classification, Burnside counting, and a pole/cycle argument. Finite computation is corroborative only. The checker independently verifies direct orbits against Burnside orbits, reproduces previously published small-side values, and brute-forces full spanning trees for \(K_{3,4}\) and \(K_{3,5}\).
scientific_limitations: The theorem fixes \(d\) and assumes \(m>d\). It proves only that the quasipolynomial period divides \(\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,d)\), not that this period is minimal. It does not cover the balanced case \(m=d\), where the bipartition classes may be exchanged by an abstract tree isomorphism. The 2008 Mohr thesis was not directly inspected; its small-side results were checked through van den Boomen (2009).
title: Quasipolynomial spanning-tree type counts for fixed-side complete bipartite graphs
